targets.title: Hodge conjecture
targets.statement: For every smooth complex projective variety, every rational Hodge class of type (p,p) is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic cycles.
proof_obligations: Handle every smooth complex projective variety and every codimension.
Construct algebraic cycle representatives with exact hypotheses.
A verified finite matrix or a special family does not establish the general conjecture.
targets.research_focus: Reviewed result in docs/HODGE-DEGREE-OBSTRUCTION.md: dense elliptic Hecke orbits have unbounded transport-graph degrees. A finite list of Hilbert-polynomial tuples for cycle representatives on Zariski-dense fibers suffices for a proper spreading argument. Seek a precise sufficient bound on representative geometry, or test whether a uniform bound on total component degree with a fixed polarization suffices by relative Chow schemes. Keep the general class and codimension fixed.

targets.title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
targets.statement: Construct nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory on four-dimensional Euclidean space for every compact simple gauge group, satisfying the required axioms, with a strictly positive mass gap.
proof_obligations: Construct the continuum theory and prove all required axioms.
Control renormalization and nontriviality uniformly at physical scales.
A finite lattice spectral gap alone is insufficient.
targets.research_focus: Reviewed result in docs/YANG-MILLS-ONE-SCALE.md: P=20T, K=5/2, y_next=20*(exp(y)-1)^2 and y0=1280000*gamma*T0^3. At y0<=1/21 the exact majorant B=127/124 gives contraction u0<=80645/80724. The permitted seed gamma*T0^3<=1/26880000 yields conditional gap log(80724/80645)/t0. This assumes the source Wightman-limit hypothesis and uniform weak-coupling seed. Seek an explicit sufficient estimate for that pressure seed at weak coupling, starting with a stated finite-volume inequality. All representation counts and volume constants must be controlled.

targets.title: Riemann hypothesis
targets.statement: Every nontrivial zero of the analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half.
proof_obligations: Prove the statement for every nontrivial zero, including unbounded heights.
Justify all analytic continuations, limits and equivalences.
A finite zero computation is insufficient.
targets.research_focus: Reviewed result in docs/RH-RECIPROCAL-COEFFICIENTS.md: for f_n(q)={q/n}, e(q)=1-sum(c_n*f_n(q)) and epsilon^2=sum_{q>=1}|e(q)|^2/(q(q+1)), inversion gives sum_{n=2}^m|c_n+mu(n)|<=epsilon*m*sqrt(4*m+1-1/(m+1)). Hence coefficient mass and squarefree support are at least 1/(1000*epsilon^2) for epsilon<=1/100. A prior model reversed this upper bound; c_n=0, epsilon=1, m=2 refutes the reversed inequality. Seek an explicit finite truncation or tail estimate for damped Mobius coefficients c_n=-mu(n)*n^(-delta), delta>0. Identify the uniform estimate needed as delta tends to zero. Coefficientwise convergence alone gives no norm convergence.

targets.title: Reflexive-polytope descent D4 and proposed bound 24
targets.statement: Assess the proposed upper bound D_4 <= 24 for the maximum shortest reflexive-cover descent depth across four-dimensional reflexive polytopes. The exact value requires matching bounds.
proof_obligations: Define the genuine cover relation and verify every descent step.
Supply complete coverage of the classification with bounds at most 24.
A bound of 50 or 346 does not establish a bound of 24; matching lower bounds are required for an exact value.
targets.research_focus: The pinned census in data/d4-coverage.json has 358101083 four-dimensional reflexive polytopes in 64022 point-count pairs with raw pair bound above 24. The source reports 22<=D4<=50. A result of 24 requires genuine reflexive-cover chains and full classification coverage. Seek one exact descent lemma or a certificate that improves a specific uncovered pair. State what classification data it needs and avoid replacing cover relations by arbitrary inclusions.

targets.title: D4 lattice and the 24-point kissing configuration
targets.statement: Verify the 24 D4 root vectors form a kissing configuration in dimension four. Distinguish this construction from a universal upper bound or uniqueness theorem.
proof_obligations: Verify all 24 vectors have the same norm and every distinct pair satisfies the angular separation condition.
An optimality proof additionally rules out all configurations with at least 25 points.
Attribute existing optimality and uniqueness results; reconstructing a known configuration is not a new breakthrough.
targets.research_focus: The 24-root construction and all 276 pair separations are independently checked. Universal optimality and uniqueness are existing results. Seek a short exact geometric lemma useful for the separate packing problem, explicitly identifying its additional hypotheses. The partial-contact result in docs/D4-PARTIAL-CONTACTS.md proves containment of the reference 24-cell with 22 exact root contacts, and with 21 contacts except 96 signed-star or signed-triangle deletion sets.

targets.title: Four-dimensional sphere packing and the 24-cell bound
targets.statement: Prove that no packing of unit balls in four-dimensional Euclidean space has upper density exceeding pi^2/16, attained by the scaled D4 lattice.
proof_obligations: Cover arbitrary centers in R^4, including nonperiodic packings and centers off a fixed grid.
For a Voronoi proof, justify passing to saturated packings and a uniform lower bound of 8 for every central cell, including nonroot directions and multiple extra centers.
For a density proof using a different method, control the asymptotic density uniformly over translated windows.
targets.research_focus: Reviewed results in docs/D4-INTERMEDIATE-GRID.md give sharp density pi^2/(36*mu^4) for arbitrary selections of sites on mu*D4 when sqrt(2/3)<=mu<1, and classify periodic equality cases. Unrestricted off-grid packings remain. In docs/D4-RADIAL-SHELL.md, one center on each root ray at radius >=2 plus near extras on reference vertex rays with pairwise NONPOSITIVE inner products gives central Voronoi volume >=8. This includes inner products -1, -1/2 and 0. Seek a precise next local lemma for two vertex-ray extras with inner product +1/2, enforcing their pairwise packing and protecting gained regions from both bisectors. State the exact unresolved inequality if the argument fails.
